texts.label: A
fehler: "Kindness leaves the heat on. I read that somewhere." – a cute aphorism that explains the scene's emotion instead of showing it
"because people came here for the worst reasons" – a mildly explanatory narrator comment
"I'm sorry," she said, "I—" – this should be two sentences: "she said. "I—"
"She stopped." – she has already come in and spoken, so there is no movement left to stop
The dead wife from March, a familiar grief-visit motif, edges close to a revelation

texts.label: B
fehler: "as if he'd been saying it silently for some time" – slightly over-interpreted
"She should call security." – a familiar beat, though handled briefly
"Her badge hung turned against her hip" – "turned against" is a little vague

texts.label: C
fehler: "the ordinary machinery of people keeping one another alive" – a sentimental, explanatory summary
"Sir, visiting hours are over." – a stock line, and an odd one for a chapel
"Lena considered calling security." – a conventional beat
"I was told to sit here." / "I don't remember." – mystery for its own sake, with no weight behind it
Somewhat over the target length (~300 words) and flat in rhythm

texts.label: D
fehler: Clearly over length (~370 instead of ~250 words)
"the chapel was dark except for the lamp over the altar" – a logic gap: nobody switched off the light
"pushed the hymnal back into its slot" – the hymnal was never introduced before
"the door sighed shut" – a worn-out image
"out of a habit she didn't examine" – thin motivation for detouring into the chapel with a water pitcher

texts.label: E
fehler: "A long grey hair was still wound through its teeth." – a pointed reveal ending that functions as a revelation, contrary to the brief
The hair still in the comb since March is implausible and sentimental
"waiting for someone" – a symbolically overloaded line about the tissue box
"the kind of tidy that takes effort at that hour" – a slightly mannered phrase
Somewhat over the target length (~290 words)
